title: Framework must have WAI-Spoke/commands/ as real file copies, not symlinks

content.what: The framework repo was missing WAI-Spoke/commands/ entirely. When we added it as symlinks, the user correctly identified this as synthetic — symlinks bypass the teaching application process (prerequisite greps pass without the teaching ever being applied). Real file copies were created instead, kept in sync via shipit Step 1.
content.why_it_matters: The framework must face identical workflows to any spoke. If it uses synthetic shortcuts (symlinks), it stops being a valid test of its own protocols. Teaching prerequisite checks test whether a file has RECEIVED a teaching — symlinks make every check trivially pass.
content.behavioral_implication: WAI-Spoke/commands/ in the framework is a real directory with real file copies. Shipit Step 1 syncs templates/commands/ -> WAI-Spoke/commands/ at every production closeout. Teachings applied to the framework target WAI-Spoke/commands/ as the spoke instance, and separately update templates/commands/ as the canonical source.
content.challenge_solved: Framework was not dogfooding its own spoke structure. Structural gap caused teaching prerequisite checks to fail silently (file not found), making teaching application seem blocked when canonical content was actually current.

_behavior_directive.what_this_is: Architectural principle: framework must use real file copies in WAI-Spoke/commands/, not symlinks or synthetic workarounds.
_behavior_directive.what_this_is_NOT: An instruction to restructure templates/ or change the canonical source location.
